title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Longue Marche period, early 1981; Grothendieck's own page number 23). The previous page proposes treating the huge groups Gamma_K (K a finitely generated extension of Q) as limits of the groups pi_1 of affine models U of K. It singles out models that are 'elementary' anabelian varieties (successive fibrations in hyperbolic curves), or more generally profinite K(pi,1)s, and suggests adding compatibility with 'modular filtrations' to the Hom-conjecture for fields.

This page makes four moves.

(1) Programme. Besides finitely generated extensions of Q and the homomorphisms of their absolute Galois groups, one should study the analogous problem for elementary anabelian models, and even general K(pi,1) models. Models over a base field K of finite type over Q (mixed situations) are set aside as 'bâtardes' for the moment.

(2) Functoriality. If U, V are such models over Q, a morphism V -> U induces a morphism of étale topoi over B_Q. Equivalently, it induces an outer homomorphism E_V = pi_1(V) -> E_U = pi_1(U) compatible with the projections to Gamma_Q. (The page writes B_U -> B_V, presumably a slip for B_V -> B_U.)

(3) Rigidity remark. If U is elementary anabelian, the morphism V -> U is already determined by the induced map on geometric l-adic homology H_1(V-bar, Z_l) -> H_1(U-bar, Z_l). This abelian, geometric datum is far less than the isomorphism class of the morphism of B_Q-topoi. He then sharpens the statement: it suffices that the target embeds in an abelian (in modern terms semi-abelian) variety. The underlying argument is Albanese-type:
- f, g : V -> A with the same map on T_l differ by a map V -> A that is zero on H_1, hence constant.
- If the image is a hyperbolic curve U inside its generalized Jacobian, the stabilizer of U under translation is trivial, so f = g.

(4) The real question. Which homomorphisms B_V -> B_U (or E_V -> E_U) come from morphisms of varieties? This leads on the next page to the 'Conjecture fondamentale', the relative Hom-conjecture: for V regular of finite type and U elementary anabelian, a Gamma_Q-compatible outer homomorphism comes from a unique morphism V -> U iff its restriction to the geometric pi_1 is 'anabelian', i.e. images of open subgroups have trivial centralizer.
errors: Directions of arrows are reversed: a morphism V -> U induces B_V -> B_U and H_1(V-bar) -> H_1(U-bar), not B_U -> B_V and H_1(U-bar) -> H_1(V-bar) as written.

The rigidity claim fails for constant morphisms. Distinct rational points of U give constant maps V -> U with the same (zero) map on H_1, so a non-constancy or dominance hypothesis is needed. The next page's anabelian (trivial-centralizer) condition implicitly excludes this case.

For higher-dimensional elementary anabelian U, H_1 does not in general determine maps. For a Kodaira-type fibration with no fixed part, Alb(U) = Alb(base), so U -> Alb(U) is not injective. Grothendieck's parenthetical restriction to targets embeddable in an (semi-)abelian variety repairs this; it is not automatic for 'elementary anabelian'.

ideas.what: Extend the birational (field) anabelian programme to elementary anabelian models and general profinite K(pi,1) models over Q; regard models over a finitely generated base field as 'bastard' mixed situations
ideas.modern_name: anabelian geometry of hyperbolic polycurves / K(pi,1) varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); later Hoshi, Mochizuki, Schmidt–Stix for polycurves and higher dimension
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Morphisms of varieties induce morphisms of étale topoi over B_Q, i.e. Gamma_Q-compatible outer homomorphisms of pi_1
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of the étale fundamental group / étale topos

ideas.what: A non-constant morphism into a variety embeddable in a (semi-)abelian variety is determined by its effect on l-adic H_1 of the geometric fibre
ideas.modern_name: Albanese rigidity / injectivity of Hom into T_l

ideas.what: Question of characterizing which homomorphisms of étale topoi / fundamental groups come from morphisms, leading to the relative Hom-conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983); proved for hyperbolic curve targets by Mochizuki (1999, sub-p-adic fields)

missed.claim: This is a pre-1983 draft stage of the Hom-conjecture of the Faltings letter. It also contains the explicit observation that, for targets embeddable in an abelian variety, abelianized geometric data already pin down the morphism. That contrasts with the full nonabelian Galois-compatible datum needed to recognize which homomorphisms are geometric. This is historically informative but mathematically classical.
missed.quote: est connu quand on connaît seulement H_1(B_Ū, Z_ℓ) → H_1(B_V̄, Z_ℓ) – ce qui est beaucoup moins que la classe d'isom. du hom. de B_Q-topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the genesis of the relative Hom-conjecture. It shows Grothendieck separating uniqueness (cheap, via Albanese) from existence (the hard anabelian part), much as Mochizuki's proof does.

deep.surprise_reason: Programmatic page preparing the Hom-conjecture later stated in the Faltings letter. The rigidity remark is classical Albanese theory, with a gap for constant maps. No new finished result.
transcription_corrections: Bars on the H_1 terms: the image reads H_1(B_Ū, Z_ℓ) → H_1(B_V̄, Z_ℓ) (geometric fibres), with the overbars on U and V.
'{+K cat.[?]+}' replacing 'de nombres' is uncertain; the reading suggests something like 'K arb.' (arbitraire) or 'K car. 0'.

In the parenthetical, the image appears to read '(En fait, [il s'applique crossed out] ... anabélien sur V, dès que V se plonge dans une VA, f est connu quand on connaît son action sur les topos ét.les ...)'. Mathematically the embedding condition should concern the target U, so 'V' may be a slip or misreading.
'morphisme de topos galoisiens[?]' is uncertain in the image; given the next page ('topos étales sur Q'), 'topos étales' is the more plausible reading.
Duplicated 'pour' in 'mais pour pour le moment' is a transcription artifact.
